title: Capacity convexity 1:1 prep — pool-level scenarios
content:
Purpose: quick prep for 1:1 with Priya (capacity lead) and follow-up tracker. Trying to capture scenario thinking (convex cost/latency tradeoffs) so we can lock reservation mix before mid-quarter commit. Not polished — working notes and action items.

Meeting goals (10–15 min):
- Align on Q2 reserve posture across p3/p4 families (commit mix target).
- Agree autoscaling headroom policy and burst budget for irregular spikes.
- Identify 2 short experiments we can run to improve utilization before next billing cycle.

Background/context:
- Last quarter we saw a pattern: steady growth in embedding workloads (batch) + spiky chat traffic (low-latency). Current reserved capacity: 120 p3-equivalent GPUs, with 25% of peak usage still served via burst pools. Cost leakage from small chat spikes => preemptible churn.
- Constraint: procurement/finance wants a binding commit decision by 2026-03-15 for the next 12-month window.

Key trade-offs to surface (for 1:1):
- Reservation vs burst: commit more to lower unit-cost but increase wasted capacity if growth stalls. Keep more on-demand to remain flexible but higher unit cost.
- Autoscale aggressiveness: faster scale-up reduces tail latency but increases cost due to cold-starts and smaller sustained usage inefficiency.
- Quantization/packing: increasing quantization may allow more effective GPUs but impacts model quality — map to QoS budgets per customer tier.

Scenario sketches (high level) — pick one during meeting:
1) Conservative commit (low risk): +10% reserved (132 p3-eq) with 30% burst budget. Autoscale threshold: scale when 80% sustained for 60s. Runway: ~9 months of comfortable buffer if growth flat.
2) Balanced commit (preferred): +25% reserved (150 p3-eq), reduce burst to 15%. Autoscale threshold: scale at 85% sustained for 30s, cold-burst throttle for ephemeral <5s spikes. Expected cost reduction on token unit by ~12% but requires 8–10% utilization improvement to break even.
3) Aggressive commit (growth bet): +50% reserved (180 p3-eq) with 5% burst. Autoscale threshold: 90% sustained for 15s (aggressive packing). High upside if volume grows but ~3–4 months runway risk if growth stalls.

Short quantitative checklist (numbers to confirm before meeting):
- Current 7-day average p3-eq utilization: 62% (confirm from console).
- Peak observed last 30 days: 215 p3-eq peak-minute.
- Median session length for chat requests: 350 tokens (~1.2s generator time).
- Batch embedding average token rate: 4M tokens/hour during batch windows.
- Current burst spend monthly: $42k (need latest invoice).

Autoscaling policy proposals (ops-focused):
- Node group fast-path: allow ephemeral scale-up using burst-capacity until 10% of reserved is free, then start moving traffic to reserved nodes.
- Graceful fallback: if reserved pool < 60% healthy, redirect non-SLA traffic (background batch) to queued processing with best-effort retries.
- Prefetch/KV cache sizing: maintain LRU cache with target hit rate 72% for top-requested prefixes to avoid repeated token compute during scale-ups.

Experiment backlog (pick 2):
- Trial A: aggressive prefix caching for top-50 customer prompts (target +8% effective tokens saved). Owner: Aisha. Timeline: 4 weeks.
- Trial B: mixed-precision packaging on p4 for low-sensitivity models (monitor quality drift). Owner: Samir. Timeline: 6 weeks.
- Trial C: burst-throttle smoothing — limit burst allocations to a 60s rolling window, measure tail latency and cost. Owner: Morgan. Timeline: 3 weeks.

Risks & open questions:
- Finance appetite: what discount threshold triggers auto-approval? Need alignment with Priya and Fiona in finance.
- Model quality impact from quantization: where do we draw the line for enterprise customers with strict regen tests? Need to wire evaluate harness.
- Hardware mix mismatch: some customers require p4 features — how do we map those reservations explicitly in SKU mix?

Agenda draft for 1:1:
- 0:00–0:02 quick status: utilization & peak numbers (I present).
- 0:02–0:06 discuss preferred reservation scenario (Conservative / Balanced / Aggressive).
- 0:06–0:10 autoscale guardrails and burst budget decision.
- 0:10–0:12 pick experiments to kick off.
- 0:12–0:15 assign owners & agree next sync / decision timeline.

Post-meeting expected outputs (I will draft):
- Short decision memo (1 paragraph) summarizing chosen scenario, autoscale thresholds, and burst budget — circulate to Finance & CTO.
- Ticket(s) created in Jira: reservation-commit, autoscale-policy-change, experiments backlog.
- Dashboard snapshot saved to Confluence with utilization & cost delta projections for chosen scenario.

Immediate action items (pre-meeting):
- Morgan: pull last 30d minute-level utilization and confirm 7d average (due: EOD before meeting).
- Aisha: sanity-check embedding batch volume numbers (due: before meeting).
- Samir: surface any model quality red flags for p4 quantization (due: before meeting).
- Priya: confirm finance deadline and any discount thresholds we need to hit (asked via Slack).

Post-meeting follow-ups (assignments to add to Jira):
- Reserve-commit-ticket: create draft with selected SKU mix and timelines (Owner: Priya / Morgan).
- Autoscale-policy-change: implement staged config and safety rollbacks (Owner: SRE oncall).
- Experiment-A/B: kickoff tickets with data collection metrics and success criteria (Owners assigned above).

Notes to self: keep the decision conservative enough to survive a plateau but structured so we can expand into aggressive commit if signals arrive (week-over-week growth >8% for 4 consecutive weeks). Watch for commit cliff dates and ensure we have a short-term swap plan (marketplace burst) if we need to unwind.

Slack snippets to paste to Priya: 
"Quick sync: prepping 1:1 for reserve decision. Leaning toward Balanced (+25% reserved) unless finance wants lower capex. Can you confirm procurement cutoff date and any required forecast format?"

End of note. Will refine after data pull.
